title: object-history-client: history get, destroyed query, restore over base-client SetCall
description:
Design: docs/design/object-history.md. Decisions: docs/design/DECISIONS.md.
Note key: H10. Crates: jmap-object-history-client. Size: M.

Spec: object-history-03 §3, §3.1 (no reliance on expires/hasOlder/version across requests), §4, §5.1, §8.4. Design: docs/design/object-history.md §8; docs/design/conditional.md §8 (SetCall, set_call); decision 8.

Work:
- Sealed JmapObjectHistoryExt::with_object_history_session(session) -> SessionClient, mail-client canonical shape. Uses OHT types directly, with no re-exports.
- supports::<O>(cap).
- Generic get_history::<O>(&HistoryGetCall) -> GetResponse<HistoryEntry<O>>.
- query_destroyed::<O>(&DestroyedQueryCall<O>) -> QueryResponse. queryChanges is the ordinary call.
- restore::<O>(&SetCall, extra_using) builds on base-client SetCall.restore (added by conditional:C6 per decision 8). It adds JMAP_OBJECT_HISTORY_URI to extra_using, calls JmapClient::set_call and returns (SetResponse<PartialObject>, RestoreOutcome). Documented: restore may be combined with conditional options; an atomicFailure decodes through ConditionalError, and AtomicFailure::not_restored() (decision 6(b)).
- Paging helpers older_page_before (returns replaced exactly as received) and has_older.
- Rustdoc covers §8.4 and §3.1.

Acceptance:
- wiremock tests: request JSON for each call matches hand-written spec-shaped JSON, including `using`.
- RestoreOutcome decode from the §5.3 example response.
- atomicFailure with notRestored decodes.
- README/PLAN/public-api, CHANGELOG.
